parts.title: Library Registration
parts.transcript:
Librarian: Good morning, City Central Library. How can I help you? 
Man: Hello, I'd like to join the library. 
Librarian: Okay. First of all, let me get some details from you. Can I have your name? 
Man: Yes, it's Martin. 
Librarian: And your surname? 
Man: It's Cox. C-O-X. 
Librarian: Right. And your address? 
Man: Apartment 1, 72 Black Street, Highbridge. 
Librarian: Black Street... like the colour? 
Man: Yes. 
Librarian: And Highbridge is the town? 
Man: Yes. 
Librarian: Okay, and postcode? 
Man: It's HB5 8RJ. 
Librarian: Right. And can I have your date of birth, please? 
Man: 12th of July, 1988. 
Librarian: And your telephone number? 
Man: My home number is 9982 7361. 
Librarian: Okay... and now I need to see some identification. Do you have a driving licence or a passport? 
Man: I'm afraid I don't have either with me. 
Librarian: That's okay. I'll need to see some other kind of identification. Do you have a utility bill with your name and address on it? 
Man: Yes, I do. Here's my electricity bill. 
Librarian: Thank you. That's fine. So, your membership card will be ready in a few minutes. I just need to explain a few things about the library. You can borrow up to eight items at a time. That's books, CDs, or videos. You must have your membership card with you when you want to borrow items. 
Man: I see. And what about the opening hours? 
Librarian: The library is open from 9 am to 5 pm from Monday to Saturday. We are closed on Sunday morning, but open in the afternoon from 1 pm to 4 pm. 
Man: Okay. And how long can I borrow items for? 
Librarian: Books can be borrowed for three weeks. CDs and videos for one week. You can renew items if they haven't been requested by another member. You can do this by phone or online. 
Man: What happens if I return items late? 
Librarian: There's a late fee of 25 cents per book per day. 
Man: Okay. Thank you. 
Librarian: Here is your membership card. You can use it right away. 
Man: Great. Thank you very much.

parts.title: Course Discussion
parts.transcript:
Tutor: Hi Anna, come in and take a seat. 
Student: Thanks. 
Tutor: So, you've come to discuss your course choices for next semester? 
Student: Yes, that's right. I'm a bit unsure about what to take. I'm in my second year of Environmental Science. 
Tutor: Okay, let's have a look at the options. There are a few core modules you have to take. There's 'Global Ecosystems' and 'Data Analysis for Scientists'. 
Student: Right, I've already noted those down. It's the optional modules I'm not sure about. 
Tutor: There are four main choices. You can do 'Oceanography', 'Urban Greening', 'Conservation Biology', or 'Environmental Policy'. You need to choose two. 
Student: 'Oceanography' sounds interesting, but I'm not very strong in marine biology. 
Tutor: It is quite specialized. It involves a lot of chemistry and physics, which some students find challenging. What about 'Urban Greening'? 
Student: I was looking at that. It seems very practical. Does it involve any fieldwork? 
Tutor: Yes, it does. There's a project component where you have to design a green space for a local community area. It's very popular. Last year's project was at the City Hospital. 
Student: Oh, that sounds great. I think I'll definitely take that one. Now I need one more. 
Tutor: 'Conservation Biology' is a good choice if you're interested in wildlife and habitat protection. It's more theoretical. 
Student: And 'Environmental Policy'? What does that cover? 
Tutor: That's more about the laws and regulations concerning the environment. It involves a lot of reading and essay writing. It's good for students who might want to work in government or for an NGO. The assessment is a 4,000-word essay. 
Student: Hmm, I'm more interested in the practical science side than policy. I think I'll go with 'Conservation Biology'. 
Tutor: Excellent choices. 'Urban Greening' and 'Conservation Biology' will give you a good balance of practical and theoretical knowledge. Just remember that 'Urban Greening' has a group presentation as part of the assessment. 
Student: A group presentation? Okay, I'll keep that in mind. Thanks for your help. 
Tutor: You're welcome. Just fill out the form online by the end of Friday.
